name_en: Thosai (Sri Lankan Dosa / Fermented Rice Crepe)
regional_origin: Tamil Sri Lanka (Northern and Eastern provinces)

ingredients.name: Raw white rice
ingredients.notes: about 1.5 cups; long-grain or sona masoori; soaked separately from the dal for 4-6 hours

ingredients.name: Whole urad dal (black gram)
ingredients.notes: about 1/2 cup; soaked separately from the rice for 4-6 hours; the ratio of rice to urad dal determines the texture -- more rice = crispier thosai

ingredients.name: Fenugreek seeds
ingredients.notes: soaked with the urad dal; helps fermentation and adds a characteristic slight bitterness

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: cold water for grinding; use as little as possible -- a thick batter ferments better

ingredients.name: Oil
ingredients.notes: for cooking; coconut oil or sesame oil are traditional

steps.instruction: Rinse the rice and urad dal (with fenugreek) separately in several changes of water, then soak them in separate bowls of cold water for 4-6 hours or overnight.

Drain both separately. Grind the urad dal and fenugreek first with a little cold water in a wet grinder or powerful blender until very smooth, light, and fluffy -- about 10 minutes in a wet grinder, 5-8 minutes in a high-powered blender. The batter should be very smooth and slightly airy.
Grind the rice separately with a little cold water until smooth but slightly coarser than the urad dal batter.

Combine both batters in a large bowl. Mix well with your hand or a large spoon. The combined batter should be thick and pourable, similar to a thick pancake batter. Cover loosely and ferment in a warm place for 8-12 hours, or overnight, until the batter rises and small bubbles appear on the surface.
After fermentation, add the salt and mix gently. Thin the batter with a little water if needed -- it should pour and spread easily but not be watery.

Heat a flat griddle or non-stick tawa over medium-high heat until very hot. Drizzle a few drops of oil and wipe around with a folded cloth. Pour a ladle of batter into the centre of the hot griddle and immediately spread it in concentric circles using the back of the ladle to make a thin, even crepe about 20-25cm across.

Drizzle a little oil around the edges and on top. Cook for 2-3 minutes until the bottom is golden and crispy and the edges lift naturally. For a plain thosai, fold in half and serve. For a masala thosai, add a spoonful of spiced potato filling before folding.
Serve hot with coconut chutney, pol sambol, or sambar. Thosai must be eaten immediately -- they become chewy and soft if left to sit.

source_site: islandsmile.org, cross-checked against hungrylankan.com, topsrilankanrecipe.com, jaffnacuisine.com, sharmispassions.com, vegrecipesofindia.com, and Wikipedia (Dosa)
collection_method: scraped, cross-checked across 7+ independent sources from both Sri Lankan and South Indian cuisine given the shared tradition; strong agreement on the 3:1 rice-to-dal ratio for crispy thosai and overnight fermentation
notes: Thosai (also spelled dosai or dosa) is the Tamil Sri Lankan name for the South Indian dosa -- the same fermented rice-and-dal crepe eaten across South India. It is a staple breakfast in the Northern and Eastern Tamil-majority provinces and increasingly popular island-wide. The 3:1 rice-to-urad-dal ratio is the standard for a crispy plain thosai (sada thosai); some families use a 2:1 ratio for a softer, thicker texture. The fermentation period is the most critical variable: under-fermented batter produces flat, dense thosai without the characteristic tang; over-fermented batter becomes too sour and may not spread evenly. The total_time_min (500 minutes) includes 8 hours of fermentation. Sri Lankan thosai is typically thinner and crispier than the thick South Indian 'set dosa' style.
